gap_report_metadata.requirement_title: As a customer, I want to browse available mobile devices, review product details and default configurations, view promotional offers and estimated delivery information, authenticate when required, and seamlessly continue my purchase journey after successful login, so that I can make an informed purchase decision and complete my mobile device purchase successfully.

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: When the Product Details Page is opened, the application shall: Display the default device colour. Display the default storage option. Display the default payment option. Display the correct pricing for the default configuration. Display the estimated delivery date. Display the promotional offer (if available).
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify default device configuration displays correct values for Colour, Storage, and Payment option on Samsung Galaxy A57 5G details page
Verify default device configuration displays correct colour, storage, and payment option on Samsung Galaxy A57 5G PDP
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases 658 and 668 validate default colour (Black/Awesome Navy), storage (256GB), and payment option (24-month installment). However, they do not explicitly verify correct pricing for default configuration, estimated delivery date, or promotional offer display. These three critical aspects are missing from test coverage, representing a 50% gap in AC3 validation. This gap poses a risk to revenue accuracy and customer experience as pricing errors or missing delivery information could lead to customer dissatisfaction and abandoned purchases.
recommended_test_enhancements: Add explicit validation step to verify correct pricing calculation and display based on default configuration (colour, storage, payment option). Include test data with expected price values for each configuration combination.

Add validation step to verify estimated delivery date visibility, format (e.g., 'Estimated delivery: DD MMM YYYY'), and accuracy. Ensure delivery date is dynamically calculated based on current date and logistics parameters.

Add validation step to verify promotional offer display when available, including offer text, discount amount, and validity period. Also validate graceful handling when no promotional offer is active (e.g., section hidden or 'No offers available' message).
Create negative test scenarios to validate pricing display when API returns invalid/null pricing data, and verify appropriate error handling without breaking the page layout.

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: The customer shall be able to: View the Next button. Click the Next button. Continue to the next purchase step. Prevent duplicate submissions when the button is clicked multiple times. Resume the purchase journey after successful authentication.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify Next button is interactable and initiates the next step in purchase journey
Verify Next button initiates the next step in purchase journey
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases 659 and 669 validate Next button visibility, clickability, and initiation of next purchase step. Test cases 664 and 674 validate duplicate submission prevention through button disabling and rapid click handling. However, none of the test cases explicitly verify resuming the purchase journey after successful authentication, which is a critical aspect of AC4. This represents a 20% gap in AC4 coverage. The missing validation creates a risk of poor user experience where authenticated users may lose their selected configuration or be redirected to incorrect pages, leading to purchase abandonment.
recommended_test_enhancements: Create an end-to-end test case that validates the complete authentication flow: 1) User selects device configuration on PDP. 2) User clicks Next while unauthenticated. 3) Login popup appears and blocks purchase journey. 4) User successfully logs in with valid credentials. 5) System redirects user back to the exact purchase step (PDP) with selected configuration intact (device model, colour, storage, payment option preserved). 6) User can continue purchase journey seamlessly by clicking Next again.
Add validation to verify session state persistence after authentication, ensuring all user selections (device configuration, quantity, add-ons) are maintained in session storage or backend.
Add validation to verify the URL after authentication redirect matches the interrupted purchase step URL, confirming users are returned to the correct page.
Test edge cases: authentication timeout during login, authentication failure and retry, and multiple authentication attempts to ensure purchase journey resumption works consistently.

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: If the customer is not authenticated, the application shall: Display the Login popup after clicking Next. Display Login and Sign Up options. Prevent the purchase journey until authentication is completed. Redirect the customer back to the interrupted purchase step after successful login.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify login or sign-up popup is displayed with correct message and action buttons when unauthenticated user clicks Next
Verify login and sign-up popup displays with correct message and action buttons for unauthenticated user
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases 660 and 670 validate login popup display after clicking Next, presence of Login and Sign Up options, and popup message content ('Please log in or sign up to continue'). However, they do not verify that the purchase journey is prevented until authentication is completed (e.g., closing popup blocks further progress), nor do they validate redirection back to the interrupted purchase step after successful login with context preservation. This represents a 50% gap in AC5 coverage. The missing validation creates security and UX risks: users might bypass authentication, or lose their purchase context after login, leading to frustration and cart abandonment.
recommended_test_enhancements: Add validation step to verify purchase journey is blocked when user attempts to close or dismiss the login popup without authenticating. Verify that clicking outside the popup, pressing ESC key, or clicking a close button does not allow the user to proceed to the next purchase step.
Add validation step to verify that after closing the popup without authentication, clicking Next button again re-displays the login popup, confirming persistent authentication enforcement.

Create end-to-end test case: 1) User clicks Next on PDP while unauthenticated. 2) Login popup appears. 3) User clicks 'Log in with Hub ID' and enters valid credentials. 4) User completes login successfully. 5) System redirects user back to Samsung Galaxy A57 5G PDP with selected configuration preserved (colour, storage, payment option intact). 6) User can now click Next and proceed to the next purchase step without re-authentication.
Add validation to verify authentication token/session is properly established after login and persists across subsequent purchase steps.
Test negative scenarios: login failure handling, network interruption during authentication, and session expiry during purchase journey to ensure robust authentication flow.

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: The application shall gracefully handle error scenarios including: Network interruption while loading pages. Device unavailability or out-of-stock condition. Slow network response while loading the Product Details Page. HTTP 500/Internal Server Error. API timeout while retrieving product details. Display appropriate error messages without crashing.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify system behavior when user attempts to navigate to All Phones with network interruption
Verify system behavior when All Phones listing page fails to load or displays zero items
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases 661 and 671 validate network interruption handling during navigation and device listing failure scenarios with appropriate error messages. Test cases 662 and 672 validate device unavailability/out-of-stock conditions with proper messaging. Test case 663 validates slow network response while loading PDP with loading indicators. However, explicit test cases for HTTP 500/Internal Server Error and API timeout while retrieving product details are not present. This represents a 33% gap in AC6 coverage. The missing validation creates a risk of poor error handling for critical server-side failures, potentially leading to application crashes, blank pages, or confusing error states that frustrate users and damage brand reputation.
recommended_test_enhancements: Create test case to validate HTTP 500/Internal Server Error handling when loading PDP or device listing: 1) Simulate HTTP 500 response from product details API. 2) Verify application displays user-friendly error message (e.g., 'We're experiencing technical difficulties. Please try again later.'). 3) Verify error message includes actionable options (Retry button, Return to Home link). 4) Verify application does not crash or display technical stack traces. 5) Verify page layout remains intact with error message displayed in appropriate location.

Create test case to validate API timeout handling when retrieving product details: 1) Simulate API timeout (e.g., response time > 30 seconds). 2) Verify application displays timeout error message (e.g., 'Request timed out. Please check your connection and try again.'). 3) Verify retry mechanism is available and functional. 4) Verify graceful degradation: if product details cannot be loaded, display cached data or partial information with clear indication of missing data. 5) Verify application remains responsive and does not freeze.
Add validation to verify error logging and monitoring: ensure HTTP 500 and timeout errors are logged to backend monitoring systems for debugging and alerting.
Test error recovery: after displaying HTTP 500 or timeout error, verify that clicking Retry button successfully reloads the page/data when the error condition is resolved.
Test combinations: simulate multiple error conditions in sequence (e.g., network interruption followed by HTTP 500) to ensure robust error handling across scenarios.
